recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-31840 unless a future BRR decision changes the allowed datatypes for SubstanceDefinition.relationship.amount[x].
issue_request: FHIR-31840 was a Published/Persuasive BRR change request for FHIR-core SubstanceSpecification asking why SubstanceDefinition.relationship.amount[x] offered both Ratio and Range ways to express the same relationship amount. The accepted resolution was that the Range flavor was not necessary.
initial_application: The Jira comment trail says the change was applied in the R4B branch and main build. Git history confirms this with ce37f02eff61835a269ba4dc378151fd7629b5f7, which removed the Range type from SubstanceDefinition.relationship.amount[x], followed by b5d679444e97f57f108c15ca403309b9ae819d56 carrying the same removal while making adjacent SubstanceDefinition property changes.
additional_context: SubstanceDefinition is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition for SubstanceDefinition.relationship.amount[x] allows Quantity, Ratio, and string, but not Range. A remaining Range type in the same resource belongs to SubstanceDefinition.property.value[x], a different element, and does not conflict with this issue. Jira searches found no later conflicting issue about SubstanceDefinition.relationship.amount[x]; Zulip had no relevant hits; Confluence BRR minutes show FHIR-31840 was moved to block vote 2 before the Jira vote.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch because the authoritative current source already reflects the accepted resolution for the target element.
